html:
Roman senator, general and engineer, best known for his book on the aqueducts of Rome.

He was a "new man", the first of his family in the Senate, and rose to be consul three times. As governor of Britain in the 70s CE he conquered the Silures of south Wales, before handing over to Agricola. He wrote a book of military tricks, the Strategemata, drawn from Greek and Roman history.

In 97 CE the emperor Nerva made him water commissioner of Rome. Frontinus studied the system closely and wrote De aquaeductu, "On the Aqueducts". It lists each aqueduct, from the Aqua Marcia to the Aqua Claudia, with its source, length and flow. It also exposes fraud: illegal pipes tapped by landowners and water men taking bribes.

It is the main source on how Roman aqueducts were run. He served as consul again under Trajan and died around 103 CE.
sum: Roman senator, general and engineer, best known for his book on the aqueducts of Rome.
